weather.headline: High Surf Warning issued November 12 at 2:47AM PST until November 15 at 4:00AM PST by NWS Eureka CA
weather.description:
* WHAT...Dangerously large breaking waves 30 to 35 ft.

* WHERE...Southwestern Humboldt and Coastal Mendocino Counties.

* WHEN...From 4 PM Friday to 4 AM PST Sunday. .

* IMPACTS...Breaking waves can sweep people off jetties and
docks, and into dangerous seas. Life-threatening surf
conditions and significant beach erosion can be expected.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...After only brief improvement late
Saturday through Sunday, a second large swell is forecast late
Sunday through Monday.
weather.instruction:
Large breaking waves along the coast will lead to increased wave
run-up on beaches with waves topping and washing over large rocks
and jetties. These large waves can be erratic and unpredictable.
Use extra caution near the surf zone as these large waves will be
capable of sweeping people into the frigid and turbulent ocean
water. Mariners traversing the bar are urged to exercise extreme
caution or stay in port until the threat subsides. Please contact
the U.S. Coast Guard for information regarding harbor and bar
closures.

events.title: High Surf Warning
events.description: * WHAT...For the Beach Hazards Statement, An increased risk for sneaker waves and strong rip currents with breaking waves of 15 to 20 ft expected. For the High Surf Warning, Dangerously large breaking waves of 25 to 35 ft, with occasional sets of 40 to 50 ft at favored breakpoints. For the Coastal Flood Advisory, large breaking waves will run up beaches and crash over seawalls, inundating adjacent, low-lying infrastructure. * WHERE...Coastal North Bay Including Point Reyes National Seashore, San Francisco Peninsula Coast and Northern Monterey Bay. * WHEN...For the Beach Hazards Statement, through Friday afternoon. For the High Surf Warning, from 6 PM Friday to 4 AM PST Sunday. For the Coastal Flood Advisory, from midnight Friday night to 6 PM PST Saturday. * IMPACTS...High tides will result in flooding of low-lying infrastructure, isolated road closures, and coastal erosion. Rising tides will bring water and waves farther up the beach than normal, restricting escape from beaches and coastal areas. Dangerously large breaking waves can overpower swimmers, pulling people into the sea from beaches, jetties, and rocks resulting in significant physical injury and increasing the risk of drowning. Waves can sweep across the shoreline without warning, pulling people into the sea from beaches, jetties, and rocks. * ADDITIONAL DETAILS...The Coastal Flood Advisory on Saturday is specifically for the Pacific Coast, where large breaking waves will spill over sea walls and run up beaches onto adjacent infrastructure.

location.region: Coastal North Bay Including Point Reyes National Seashore; San Francisco Peninsula Coast; Northern Monterey Bay

events.title: High Surf Warning
events.description: * WHAT...For the Beach Hazards Statement, An increased risk for sneaker waves and strong rip currents with breaking waves of 15 to 20 ft expected. For the High Surf Warning, Dangerously large breaking waves of 25 to 35 ft, with occasional sets of 40 to 50 ft at favored breakpoints. For the Coastal Flood Advisory, large breaking waves will run up beaches and crash over seawalls, inundating adjacent, low-lying infrastructure. * WHERE...Coastal North Bay Including Point Reyes National Seashore, San Francisco Peninsula Coast and Northern Monterey Bay. * WHEN...For the Beach Hazards Statement, through Friday afternoon. For the High Surf Warning, from 6 PM Friday to 4 AM PST Sunday. For the Coastal Flood Advisory, from midnight Friday night to 6 PM PST Saturday. * IMPACTS...High tides will result in flooding of low-lying infrastructure, isolated road closures, and coastal erosion. Rising tides will bring water and waves farther up the beach than normal, restricting escape from beaches and coastal areas. Dangerously large breaking waves can overpower swimmers, pulling people into the sea from beaches, jetties, and rocks resulting in significant physical injury and increasing the risk of drowning. Waves can sweep across the shoreline without warning, pulling people into the sea from beaches, jetties, and rocks. * ADDITIONAL DETAILS...The Coastal Flood Advisory on Saturday is specifically for the Pacific Coast, where large breaking waves will spill over sea walls and run up beaches onto adjacent infrastructure.

location.region: Coastal North Bay Including Point Reyes National Seashore; San Francisco Peninsula Coast; Northern Monterey Bay

events.title: High Surf Warning
events.description: * WHAT...For the first Coastal Flood Advisory, Up to 1.5 ft of inundation above ground level is possible in low-lying areas near shorelines and tidal waterways. For the Beach Hazards Statement, An increased risk for sneaker waves and strong rip currents with breaking waves of 15 to 20 ft expected. For the High Surf Warning, Dangerously large breaking waves of 25 to 35 ft, with occasional sets of 40 to 50 ft at favored breakpoints. For the second Coastal Flood Advisory, large breaking waves will run up beaches and crash over seawalls, inundating adjacent, low-lying infrastructure. * WHERE...San Francisco and Southern Monterey Bay and Big Sur Coast. * WHEN...For the first Coastal Flood Advisory, until 4 PM PST Friday. For the Beach Hazards Statement, through Friday afternoon. For the High Surf Warning, from 6 PM Friday to 4 AM PST Sunday. For the second Coastal Flood Advisory, from midnight Friday night to 6 PM PST Saturday. * IMPACTS...High tides will result in flooding of low-lying infrastructure, isolated road closures, and coastal erosion. Rising tides will bring water and waves farther up the beach than normal, restricting escape from beaches and coastal areas. Dangerously large breaking waves can overpower swimmers, pulling people into the sea from beaches, jetties, and rocks resulting in significant physical injury and increasing the risk of drowning. Waves can sweep across the shoreline without warning, pulling people into the sea from beaches, jetties, and rocks. * ADDITIONAL DETAILS...At the San Francisco tide gauge, high tide is expected to be: 1.5 ft above normal (7.3 ft MLLW) at 12:49 PM Friday 11/13. These predictions include up to 1.8 ft of surge that will enhance the astronomical tide and flooding threat. High tide varies up to 90 minutes earlier or later along the Pacific Coast and through the San Francisco Bay, respectively. The Coastal Flood Advisory on Saturday is specifically for the Pacific Coast, where large breaking waves will spill over sea walls and run up beaches onto adjacent infrastructure.

events.title: Flood Watch
events.description: * WHAT...Flooding caused by excessive rainfall continues to be possible. * WHERE...A portion of northwest Washington, including the following county, Mason. * WHEN...From late tonight through late Saturday night. * IMPACTS...Excessive runoff may result in flooding of rivers, creeks, streams, and other low-lying and flood-prone locations. * ADDITIONAL DETAILS... - Three to four and a half inches of rain is forecast for the south slopes of the Olympics between early Friday and early Sunday with snow levels of 5500 to 6500 feet. The combination of heavy rain and relatively high snow levels could push the Skokomish River near Potlatch above flood stage. - http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood

events.title: High Surf Warning
events.description: * WHAT...For the first Coastal Flood Advisory, Up to 1.5 ft of inundation above ground level is possible in low-lying areas near shorelines and tidal waterways. For the Beach Hazards Statement, An increased risk for sneaker waves and strong rip currents with breaking waves of 15 to 20 ft expected. For the High Surf Warning, Dangerously large breaking waves of 25 to 35 ft, with occasional sets of 40 to 50 ft at favored breakpoints. For the second Coastal Flood Advisory, large breaking waves will run up beaches and crash over seawalls, inundating adjacent, low-lying infrastructure. * WHERE...San Francisco and Southern Monterey Bay and Big Sur Coast. * WHEN...For the first Coastal Flood Advisory, until 4 PM PST today. For the Beach Hazards Statement, through this afternoon. For the High Surf Warning, from 6 PM today to 4 AM PST Sunday. For the second Coastal Flood Advisory, from midnight tonight to 6 PM PST Saturday. * IMPACTS...High tides will result in flooding of low-lying infrastructure, isolated road closures, and coastal erosion. Rising tides will bring water and waves farther up the beach than normal, restricting escape from beaches and coastal areas. Dangerously large breaking waves can overpower swimmers, pulling people into the sea from beaches, jetties, and rocks resulting in significant physical injury and increasing the risk of drowning. Waves can sweep across the shoreline without warning, pulling people into the sea from beaches, jetties, and rocks. * ADDITIONAL DETAILS...At the San Francisco tide gauge, high tide is expected to be: 1.5 ft above normal (7.3 ft MLLW) at 12:49 PM today 11/13. These predictions include up to 1.8 ft of surge that will enhance the astronomical tide and flooding threat. High tide varies up to 90 minutes earlier or later along the Pacific Coast and through the San Francisco Bay, respectively. The Coastal Flood Advisory on Saturday is specifically for the Pacific Coast, where large breaking waves will spill over sea walls and run up beaches onto adjacent infrastructure.

events.title: High Surf Advisory
events.description: * WHAT...For the High Surf Advisory, large breaking waves of 5 to 8 feet today, increasing to 8 to 12 feet Saturday. Surf heights are expected to decrease to 5 to 9 feet Sunday through Tuesday. Dangerous rip currents expected. For the Coastal Flood Advisory, minor to moderate coastal flooding expected. * WHERE...Malibu Coast and Los Angeles County Beaches. Surf will we highest for west-northwest facing beaches. * WHEN...For the High Surf Advisory, until 3 PM PST Tuesday. For the Coastal Flood Advisory, from 4 AM to 4 PM PST Saturday. * IMPACTS...Moderate flooding of sea water is likely over some vulnerable low-lying coastal areas that are normally dry, especially around the time of high tide, including over beach parking lots, bike paths, and harbor walkways. Moderate to significant beach erosion is likely. Isolated damage is unlikely but possible. There is an increased risk for ocean drowning. Rip currents can pull swimmers and surfers out to sea. Large breaking waves can cause injury, wash people off beaches and rocks, and capsize small boats near shore. * ADDITIONAL DETAILS...A series of significant west- northwesterly swells are expected to produce large surf into next week with highest surf and greatest impacts likely peaking Saturday and potentially again Monday. Minor to moderate coastal flooding impacts are possible, especially when largest surf overlaps with peak high tides. Some of these impacts may be moderate to significant beach erosion and shallow flooding of normally dry beaches and walkways.

location.region: Malibu Coast; Los Angeles County Beaches

weather.description:

Rip currents can pull swimmers and surfers out to sea. Large
breaking waves can cause injury, wash people off beaches and

events.title: High Surf Warning
events.description: * WHAT...For the High Surf Advisory, large breaking waves of 10 to 15 feet with dangerous rip currents. For the High Surf Warning, dangerously large breaking waves of 18 to 25 feet with dangerous rip currents. For the Coastal Flood Warning, moderate to significant coastal flooding expected. * WHERE...San Luis Obispo County Beaches and Santa Barbara County Central Coast Beaches. Surf will we highest for west- northwest facing beaches. * WHEN...For the High Surf Advisory, until 9 PM PST this evening. For the High Surf Warning, from 9 PM this evening to 3 AM PST Sunday. For the Coastal Flood Warning, from 3 AM to 6 PM PST Saturday. * IMPACTS...There is a high risk for flooding of sea water over vulnerable low-lying coastal areas, especially around the time of high tide. This includes significant flooding of coastal beaches, walkways and roads, and potentially damaging some structures. Significant beach erosion is expected. Powerful waves and strong rip currents will pose an exceptional risk of ocean drowning and damage to coastal structures like piers and jetties. Large breaking waves can cause injury, wash people off beaches and rocks, and capsize small boats near shore. Remain far away from the water's edge. * ADDITIONAL DETAILS...A series of west-northwesterly swells will create an extended period of large surf into next week, with the potential for WARNING level surf again late Sunday night through Monday. Areas that may see most significant impacts will be west-northwest facing beaches, with widespread flooding likely at low lying areas such as at Oceano Dunes. Breaking waves may impact the Cayucos and Pismo Beach piers as well as the Morro Bay Harbor entrance.

events.title: Winter Storm Watch
events.description: * WHAT...Moderate to heavy snowfall possible. * WHERE...Anchorage and Eagle River (all elevations), East Turnagain Arm, Western Kenai Peninsula, Southern Kenai Mtns, Interior Kenai Peninsula, and Turnagain Pass. * WHEN...From Saturday afternoon through late Sunday night. * IMPACTS...Travel could be very difficult. * ADDITIONAL DETAILS...Longwave troughing in the Bering Sea hedges east as inverted troughing in the Gulf of Alaska tracks west. A snow band will set up and stall over Anchorage/Kenai Peninsula tomorrow afternoon through Sunday bringing rounds of moderate to heavy snowfall. There is moderate uncertainty as to where the snow band will ultimately end up, resulting in lower confidence for snowfall amounts. events.title: High Surf Warning
events.description: * WHAT...For the Beach Hazards Statement, an increased risk for sneaker waves and strong rip currents with breaking waves of 15 to 20 ft expected. For the High Surf Warning, dangerously large breaking waves of 25 to 35 ft, with occasional sets of 40 to 50 ft at favored breakpoints. For the Coastal Flood Advisory, large breaking waves will run up beaches and crash over seawalls, inundating adjacent, low-lying infrastructure. * WHERE...San Francisco and Southern Monterey Bay and Big Sur Coast. * WHEN...For the Beach Hazards Statement, until 6 PM PST this evening. For the High Surf Warning, until 4 AM PST Sunday. For the Coastal Flood Advisory, from midnight tonight to 6 PM PST Saturday. * IMPACTS...High tides will result in flooding of low-lying infrastructure, isolated road closures, and coastal erosion. Rising tides will bring water and waves farther up the beach than normal, restricting escape from beaches and coastal areas. Dangerously large breaking waves can overpower swimmers, pulling people into the sea from beaches, jetties, and rocks resulting in significant physical injury and increasing the risk of drowning. Waves can sweep across the shoreline without warning, pulling people into the sea from beaches, jetties, and rocks. * ADDITIONAL DETAILS...The Coastal Flood Advisory on Saturday is specifically for the Pacific Coast, where large breaking waves will spill over sea walls and run up beaches onto adjacent infrastructure.

location.region: San Francisco; Southern Monterey Bay and Big Sur Coast

weather.headline: High Surf Warning issued November 13 at 3:53PM PST until November 15 at 4:00AM PST by NWS San Francisco CA
weather.description:
* WHAT...For the Beach Hazards Statement, an increased risk for
sneaker waves and strong rip currents with breaking waves of 15
to 20 ft expected. For the High Surf Warning, dangerously large
breaking waves of 25 to 35 ft, with occasional sets of 40 to 50
ft at favored breakpoints. For the Coastal Flood Advisory,
large breaking waves will run up beaches and crash over
seawalls, inundating adjacent, low-lying infrastructure.

* WHERE...San Francisco and Southern Monterey Bay and Big Sur
Coast.

* WHEN...For the Beach Hazards Statement, until 6 PM PST this
evening. For the High Surf Warning, until 4 AM PST Sunday. For
the Coastal Flood Advisory, from midnight tonight to 6 PM PST
Saturday.

* IMPACTS...High tides will result in flooding of low-lying
infrastructure, isolated road closures, and coastal erosion.
Rising tides will bring water and waves farther up the beach
than normal, restricting escape from beaches and coastal
areas. Dangerously large breaking waves can overpower
swimmers, pulling people into the sea from beaches, jetties,
and rocks resulting in significant physical injury and
increasing the risk of drowning. Waves can sweep across the
shoreline without warning, pulling people into the sea from
beaches, jetties, and rocks.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...The Coastal Flood Advisory on Saturday is
specifically for the Pacific Coast, where large breaking waves
will spill over sea walls and run up beaches onto adjacent
infrastructure.
weather.instruction:
If travel is required, allow extra time as some roads may be
closed. Do not drive around barricades or through water of
unknown depth. Take the necessary actions to protect flood-prone
property.

Everyone should remain out of the water due to life-threatening
surf conditions. Stay off of jetties, piers, and other waterside
infrastructure.

Stay off of jetties, piers, rocks, and other waterside
infrastructure. Remain out of the water to avoid hazardous surf
and NEVER turn your back on the ocean. Monitor local weather,
surf and tide forecasts at www.weather.gov/mtr.

events.description: * WHAT...Dangerously large breaking waves 30 to 40 feet. * WHERE...Northern Coastal Humboldt County. * WHEN...Until 4 AM PST Sunday. . * IMPACTS...Breaking waves can sweep people off jetties and docks, and into dangerous seas. Life-threatening surf conditions and significant beach erosion can be expected. * ADDITIONAL DETAILS...After only brief improvement late Saturday through Sunday, a second large swell is forecast late Sunday through Monday.

location.region: Northern Coastal Humboldt

weather.headline: High Surf Warning issued November 13 at 3:03PM PST until November 15 at 4:00AM PST by NWS Eureka CA
weather.description:
* WHAT...Dangerously large breaking waves 30 to 40 feet.

* WHERE...Northern Coastal Humboldt County.

* WHEN...Until 4 AM PST Sunday. .

* IMPACTS...Breaking waves can sweep people off jetties and
docks, and into dangerous seas. Life-threatening surf
conditions and significant beach erosion can be expected.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...After only brief improvement late
Saturday through Sunday, a second large swell is forecast late
Sunday through Monday.
weather.instruction:
Large breaking waves along the coast will lead to increased wave
run-up on beaches with waves topping and washing over large rocks
and jetties. These large waves can be erratic and unpredictable.
Use extra caution near the surf zone as these large waves will be
capable of sweeping people into the frigid and turbulent ocean
water. Mariners traversing the bar are urged to exercise extreme
caution or stay in port until the threat subsides. Please contact
the U.S. Coast Guard for information regarding harbor and bar
closures.

weather.description:

frequent gusts to 40 kt.

* WHERE...East Entrance U. S. Waters Strait Of Juan De Fuca.

experience and properly equipped vessels. It is highly
recommended that mariners without the proper experience seek safe
harbor prior to the onset of gale conditions.

events.title: High Surf Warning
events.description: * WHAT...Dangerous, large breaking waves of 20 to 25 ft this morning, increasing to a peak of 30 to 35 ft late this afternoon through Saturday morning. Another round of dangerous surf conditions is expected Sunday night, with breaking waves reaching 25 to 30 ft and persisting into Monday morning. Waves gradually diminish through Monday evening, but remain hazardous through the day. * WHERE...Beaches of South Central Oregon Coast and Curry County Coast. This includes Charleston, Port Orford, Gold Beach, and Brookings. * WHEN...Until 10 PM PST Monday. * IMPACTS...Extremely large breaking waves will create very hazardous conditions along beaches and area shorelines. Waves will inundate beaches and surge into normally dry areas. Infrastructure damage and significant beach erosion can be expected. * ADDITIONAL DETAILS...Breaking waves will briefly ease Saturday night to 15 to 20 ft, but quickly rise to dangerous heights again Sunday afternoon and evening.

events.title: High Surf Advisory
events.description: * WHAT...For the High Surf Advisory, large breaking waves of 5 to 8 feet Friday, increasing to 8 to 12 feet Saturday. Surf heights are expected to decrease to 5 to 9 feet Sunday through Tuesday. Dangerous rip currents expected. For the Coastal Flood Advisory, minor to moderate coastal flooding expected. * WHERE...Malibu Coast and Los Angeles County Beaches. Surf will we highest for west-northwest facing beaches. * WHEN...For the High Surf Advisory, until 3 PM PST Tuesday. For the Coastal Flood Advisory, from 4 AM to 4 PM PST Saturday. * IMPACTS...Moderate flooding of sea water is likely over some vulnerable low-lying coastal areas that are normally dry, especially around the time of high tide, including over beach parking lots, bike paths, and harbor walkways. Moderate to significant beach erosion is likely. Isolated damage is unlikely but possible. There is an increased risk for ocean drowning. Rip currents can pull swimmers and surfers out to sea. Large breaking waves can cause injury, wash people off beaches and rocks, and capsize small boats near shore. * ADDITIONAL DETAILS...A series of significant west- northwesterly swells are expected to produce large surf into next week with highest surf and greatest impacts likely peaking Saturday and potentially again Monday. Minor to moderate coastal flooding impacts are possible, especially when largest surf overlaps with peak high tides. Some of these impacts may be moderate to significant beach erosion and shallow flooding of normally dry beaches and walkways.

location.region: Malibu Coast; Los Angeles County Beaches

events.title: High Surf Warning
events.description: * WHAT...For the High Surf Advisory, large breaking waves of 10 to 15 feet with dangerous rip currents. For the High Surf Warning, dangerously large breaking waves of 18 to 25 feet with dangerous rip currents. For the Coastal Flood Warning, moderate to significant coastal flooding expected. * WHERE...San Luis Obispo County Beaches and Santa Barbara County Central Coast Beaches. Surf will we highest for west-northwest facing beaches. * WHEN...For the High Surf Advisory, until 9 PM PST Friday. For the High Surf Warning, from 9 PM Friday to 3 AM PST Sunday. For the Coastal Flood Warning, from 3 AM to 6 PM PST Saturday. * IMPACTS...There is a high risk for flooding of sea water over vulnerable low-lying coastal areas, especially around the time of high tide. This includes significant flooding of coastal beaches, walkways and roads, and potentially damaging some structures. Significant beach erosion is expected. Powerful waves and strong rip currents will pose an exceptional risk of ocean drowning and damage to coastal structures like piers and jetties. Large breaking waves can cause injury, wash people off beaches and rocks, and capsize small boats near shore. Remain far away from the water's edge. * ADDITIONAL DETAILS...A series of west-northwesterly swells will create an extended period of large surf into next week, with the potential for WARNING level surf again late Sunday night through Monday. Areas that may see most significant impacts will be west- northwest facing beaches, with widespread flooding likely at low lying areas such as at Oceano Dunes. Breaking waves may impact the Cayucos and Pismo Beach piers as well as the Morro Bay Harbor entrance.

events.title: Winter Storm Watch
events.description: * WHAT...Moderate to heavy snowfall possible. * WHERE...Anchorage and Eagle River (all elevations), East Turnagain Arm, Western Kenai Peninsula, Southern Kenai Mtns, Interior Kenai Peninsula, and Turnagain Pass. * WHEN...From Saturday afternoon through late Sunday night. * IMPACTS...Travel could be very difficult. * ADDITIONAL DETAILS...A snow band will set up and stall over Anchorage/Kenai Peninsula tomorrow afternoon through Sunday bringing rounds of moderate to heavy snowfall. There is moderate uncertainty as to where the snow band will ultimately end up, resulting in lower confidence for snowfall amounts. Warmer temperatures filters in Sunday afternoon from east to west, transitioning snow to rain. *Low/High end values are as follows: - Anchorage/Eagle River & western Kenai Peninsula: 2-4" (Low end)/6-10" (High end). Higher elevations: up to a foot possible. - Seward: 1-3" (Low end)/3-6" (High end). - Turnagain Pass to Moose Pass: 7 to 11" possible. - Portage: 9-11" with snowfall rates of up to 1" an hour.

water. Mariners traversing the bar are urged to exercise extreme
caution or stay in port until the threat subsides. Please contact
the U.S. Coast Guard for information regarding harbor and bar
closures.

weather.description:
...The Flood Warning continues for the following rivers in Texas...

Nueces River Near Tilden affecting McMullen County.

For the Nueces River...including Cotulla, Tilden, Three Rivers,
Mathis, Bluntzer, Calallen...Minor flooding is forecast.

* WHAT...Minor flooding is forecast.

* WHERE...Nueces River near Tilden.

* WHEN...From Saturday evening to late Monday night.

* IMPACTS...At 15.0 feet, Much of the flood plain below cotulla to
below tilden is cut off, as sloughs and peripheral channels fill.
Hunting cabins, oil field pump jacks and tank batteries flood well
away from the channel. Livestock are cut off and can drown.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 7:30 PM CST Friday the stage was 10.9 feet.
- Bankfull stage is 11.0 feet.
- Forecast...The river is expected to rise above flood stage
Saturday evening to a crest of 15.0 feet early Sunday afternoon.
It will then fall below flood stage late Monday morning.
- Flood stage is 14.0 feet.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
weather.instruction:
Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Most flood
deaths occur in vehicles.

Caution is urged when walking near riverbanks.

Please report observed flooding to local emergency services or law
enforcement and request they pass this information to the National
Weather Service when you can do so safely.

Additional information is available at www.weather.gov/crp.
weather.areaDesc: McMullen, TX

events.description: * WHAT...For the High Surf Warning, dangerously large breaking waves of 25 to 35 ft, with occasional sets of 40 to 50 ft at favored breakpoints. For the Coastal Flood Advisory, large breaking waves will run up beaches and crash over seawalls, inundating adjacent, low-lying infrastructure. * WHERE...All Pacific Coast Beaches. * WHEN...For the High Surf Warning, until 4 AM PST Sunday. For the Coastal Flood Advisory, from midnight tonight to 6 PM PST Saturday. * IMPACTS...High tides will result in flooding of low-lying infrastructure, isolated road closures, and coastal erosion. Dangerously large breaking waves can overpower swimmers, pulling people into the sea from beaches, jetties, and rocks resulting in significant physical injury and increasing the risk of drowning. Waves can sweep across the shoreline without warning, pulling people into the sea from beaches, jetties, and rocks. * ADDITIONAL DETAILS...The Coastal Flood Advisory on Saturday is specifically for the Pacific Coast, where large breaking waves will spill over sea walls and run up beaches onto adjacent infrastructure.

infrastructure, isolated road closures, and coastal erosion.

than normal, restricting escape from beaches and coastal
areas. Dangerously large breaking waves can overpower
swimmers, pulling people into the sea from beaches, jetties,
and rocks resulting in significant physical injury and
increasing the risk of drowning. Waves can sweep across the
shoreline without warning, pulling people into the sea from
beaches, jetties, and rocks.

specifically for the Pacific Coast, where large breaking waves
will spill over sea walls and run up beaches onto adjacent
infrastructure.

run-up on beaches with waves topping and washing over large rocks
and jetties. These large waves can be erratic and unpredictable.

capable of sweeping people into the frigid and turbulent ocean
water. Mariners traversing the bar are urged to exercise extreme
caution or stay in port until the threat subsides. Please contact
the U.S. Coast Guard for information regarding harbor and bar
closures.

events.description: * WHAT...For the High Surf Warning, large waves and dangerous surf conditions. Breakers up to 30 to 35 feet. For the High Surf Advisory, large waves and hazardous surf conditions. Breakers up to 23 to 28 feet. * WHERE...North and Central Coast of Oregon, and South Washington Coast. * WHEN...For the High Surf Warning, until noon PST today. For the High Surf Advisory, from noon today to 4 AM PST Monday. * IMPACTS...Destructive waves may wash over beaches, jetties, and other structures unexpectedly. People can be swept off rocks and jetties and drown while observing high surf. Severe beach erosion may destroy coastal properties and buildings. Higher than normal water run-up is expected on beaches and low- lying shoreline. * ADDITIONAL DETAILS...The threat of sneaker waves is extreme during these scenarios. Sneaker waves can suddenly knock people off of their feet and quickly pull them into the frigid ocean which may lead to serious injury or drowning. The sneaker wave threat will peak Friday evening into Friday night.

location.region: Clatsop County Coast; Tillamook County Coast; Central Coast of Oregon; South Washington Coast

weather.headline: High Surf Advisory issued November 14 at 12:53AM PST until November 16 at 4:00AM PST by NWS Portland OR
weather.description:
* WHAT...For the High Surf Warning, large waves and dangerous surf
conditions. Breakers up to 30 to 35 feet. For the High Surf
Advisory, large waves and hazardous surf conditions. Breakers up
to 23 to 28 feet.

* WHERE...North and Central Coast of Oregon, and South
Washington Coast.

* WHEN...For the High Surf Warning, until noon PST today. For
the High Surf Advisory, from noon today to 4 AM PST Monday.

* IMPACTS...Destructive waves may wash over beaches, jetties,
and other structures unexpectedly. People can be swept off
rocks and jetties and drown while observing high surf. Severe
beach erosion may destroy coastal properties and buildings.
Higher than normal water run-up is expected on beaches and low-
lying shoreline.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...The threat of sneaker waves is extreme
during these scenarios. Sneaker waves can suddenly knock people
off of their feet and quickly pull them into the frigid ocean
which may lead to serious injury or drowning. The sneaker wave
threat will peak Friday evening into Friday night.
weather.instruction:
A High Surf Warning means that high surf will affect beaches,
producing rip currents, sneaker waves and beach erosion. Stay
well back from the water's edge and be alert for exceptionally
high waves.

Keep away from large logs on the beach. Water running up on the
beach can lift or roll logs which can injure or kill someone
caught in their path.

events.description: ...The Flood Warning continues for the following rivers in Florida... St Johns River Near Astor affecting Volusia and Lake Counties. .On the St Johns River at Astor, slight rises within Minor Flood Stage are forecast this weekend into next week due to a combination of northerly winds, downstream tidal effects, and water from upstream heavy rainfall working north through the basin. For the St. Johns River...including Astor...Minor flooding is forecast. * WHAT...Minor flooding is occurring and moderate flooding is forecast. * WHERE...St Johns River near Astor. * WHEN...Until further notice. * IMPACTS...At 3.5 feet, Canals have overflowed into yards. Homes on or near Wildhog, Bonnet and Snail roads become inaccessible with several inches of water inside homes along the river and canals. Docks at Astor Bridge marina and throughout Astor are completely submerged. Bartram Rd and Holiday Circle are inaccessible with yards completely submerged. Clair Street is inaccessible. Roads flooded in South Moon Fish Camp, docks and yards at condominiums on Juno Trail and water breaches the sea wall at Blair's Jungle Den. * ADDITIONAL DETAILS... - At 9:30 AM EST Saturday the stage was 2.6 feet. - Bankfull stage is 2.0 feet. - Recent Activity...The maximum river stage in the 24 hours ending at 9:30 AM EST Saturday was 2.7 feet. - Forecast...The river is expected to rise to 3.4 feet just after midnight tonight. Additional rises are possible thereafter. - Flood stage is 2.3 feet. - http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood

events.title: High Surf Warning
events.description: * WHAT...For the High Surf Advisory, large breaking waves of 10 to 15 feet with dangerous rip currents. For the High Surf Warning, dangerously large breaking waves of 18 to 25 feet with dangerous rip currents. For the Coastal Flood Warning, moderate to significant coastal flooding expected. * WHERE...San Luis Obispo County Beaches and Santa Barbara County Central Coast Beaches. Surf will we highest for west- northwest facing beaches. * WHEN...For the High Surf Advisory, until 9 PM PST Friday. For the High Surf Warning, from 9 PM Friday to 3 AM PST Sunday. For the Coastal Flood Warning, from 3 AM to 6 PM PST Saturday. * IMPACTS...There is a high risk for flooding of sea water over vulnerable low-lying coastal areas, especially around the time of high tide. This includes significant flooding of coastal beaches, walkways and roads, and potentially damaging some structures. Significant beach erosion is expected. Powerful waves and strong rip currents will pose an exceptional risk of ocean drowning and damage to coastal structures like piers and jetties. Large breaking waves can cause injury, wash people off beaches and rocks, and capsize small boats near shore. Remain far away from the water's edge. * ADDITIONAL DETAILS...A series of west-northwesterly swells will create an extended period of large surf into next week, with the potential for WARNING level surf again late Sunday night through Monday. Areas that may see most significant impacts will be west- northwest facing beaches, with widespread flooding likely at low lying areas such as at Oceano Dunes. Breaking waves may impact the Cayucos and Pismo Beach piers as well as the Morro Bay Harbor entrance.

location.region: Coastal Del Norte; Northern Coastal Humboldt

weather.headline: High Surf Warning issued November 14 at 9:40AM PST until November 15 at 4:00AM PST by NWS Eureka CA
weather.description:
* WHAT...Dangerously large breaking waves 22 to 30 feet.

* WHERE...Coastal Del Norte and Northern Coastal Humboldt
Counties.

* WHEN...Until 4 AM PST Sunday.

* IMPACTS...Breaking waves can sweep people off jetties and
docks, and into dangerous seas. Life-threatening surf
conditions and significant beach erosion can be expected.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...After only brief improvement late
Saturday through Sunday, a second large swell is forecast late
Sunday through Monday.
weather.instruction:
Large breaking waves along the coast will lead to increased wave
run-up on beaches with waves topping and washing over large rocks
and jetties. These large waves can be erratic and unpredictable.
Use extra caution near the surf zone as these large waves will be
capable of sweeping people into the frigid and turbulent ocean
water. Mariners traversing the bar are urged to exercise extreme
caution or stay in port until the threat subsides. Please contact
the U.S. Coast Guard for information regarding harbor and bar
closures.

events.title: Marine Weather Statement
events.description: A large west to northwesterly swell is expected to produce breaking waves at the Morro Bay and Ventura Harbor entrances on Saturday. These conditions have a history of capsizing vessels of various sizes resulting in serious injury or death, even to the most experienced mariners. Mariners are urged to stay clear of these harbor entrances. For more information, contact the local harbor patrol or coast guard station...and continue to monitor NOAA Weather Radio for the latest weather information..

events.title: Flood Warning
events.description: * WHAT...Flooding caused by upstream dam release continues. * WHERE...Maricopa County in south central Arizona... Northeastern Yuma County in southwestern Arizona... * WHEN...Until 1100 AM MST Tuesday. * IMPACTS...Flooding of rivers, creeks, streams, and other low-lying and flood-prone locations is expected. Low-water crossings are likely to become inundated with water and may not be passable. * ADDITIONAL DETAILS... - At 724 PM MST, water releases from Painted Rock Dam continue with flow peaking at 3000 cfs. A streamflow gauge immediately downstream also indicated a stage of 9.93 feet. - Flooding is expected along the Gila River. - Some locations that will experience flooding include... Farmlands and low-water crossings along the Gila River. - http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood

location.region: Maricopa, AZ; Yuma, AZ

weather.headline: Flood Warning issued November 13 at 7:24PM MST until November 17 at 11:00AM MST by NWS Phoenix AZ
weather.description:
* WHAT...Flooding caused by upstream dam release continues.

* WHERE...Maricopa County in south central Arizona...
Northeastern Yuma County in southwestern Arizona...

* WHEN...Until 1100 AM MST Tuesday.

* IMPACTS...Flooding of rivers, creeks, streams, and other low-lying
and flood-prone locations is expected. Low-water crossings are
likely to become inundated with water and may not be passable.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 724 PM MST, water releases from Painted Rock Dam continue with
flow peaking at 3000 cfs. A streamflow gauge immediately
downstream  also indicated a stage of 9.93 feet.
- Flooding is expected along the Gila River.
- Some locations that will experience flooding include...
Farmlands and low-water crossings along the Gila River.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
weather.instruction:
Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Most flood
deaths occur in vehicles.

Be aware of your surroundings and do not drive on flooded roads.

events.title: High Surf Advisory
events.description: * WHAT...Large waves and hazardous surf conditions. Breakers up to 25 to 30 feet. * WHERE...North and Central Coast of Oregon, and South Washington Coast. * WHEN...Until 10 AM PST Monday. * IMPACTS...Destructive waves may wash over beaches, jetties, and other structures unexpectedly. People can be swept off rocks and jetties and drown while observing high surf. Minor beach erosion may damage coastal properties and buildings. Higher than normal water run-up is expected on beaches and low- lying shoreline. * ADDITIONAL DETAILS...The threat of sneaker waves is extreme during these scenarios. Sneaker waves can suddenly knock people off of their feet and quickly pull them into the frigid ocean which may lead to serious injury or drowning.

location.region: Clatsop County Coast; Tillamook County Coast; Central Coast of Oregon; South Washington Coast

weather.headline: High Surf Advisory issued November 14 at 11:58AM PST until November 16 at 10:00AM PST by NWS Portland OR
weather.description:
* WHAT...Large waves and hazardous surf conditions. Breakers up to
25 to 30 feet.

* WHERE...North and Central Coast of Oregon, and South
Washington Coast.

* WHEN...Until 10 AM PST Monday.

* IMPACTS...Destructive waves may wash over beaches, jetties,
and other structures unexpectedly. People can be swept off
rocks and jetties and drown while observing high surf. Minor
beach erosion may damage coastal properties and buildings.
Higher than normal water run-up is expected on beaches and low-
lying shoreline.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...The threat of sneaker waves is extreme
during these scenarios. Sneaker waves can suddenly knock people
off of their feet and quickly pull them into the frigid ocean
which may lead to serious injury or drowning.
weather.instruction:
A High Surf Advisory means that high surf will affect beaches,
producing rip currents, sneaker waves and beach erosion. Stay
well back from the water's edge and be alert for exceptionally
high waves.

Keep away from large logs on the beach. Water running up on the
beach can easily lift or roll logs which can injure or kill
someone caught in their path.

events.title: Special Weather Statement
events.description: Strong northwesterly winds have developed across Shelikof Strait and the waters around western Kodiak Island. These winds are resuspending ash from the 1912 Katmai-Novarupta eruption, causing haze and potentially trace amounts of ash accumulation. The villages of Karluk and Larsen Bay are most likely to be impacted. Those in sensitive groups or with respiratory ailments are encouraged to avoid or reduce outdoor activity to avoid inhaling the ash. The winds should weaken Saturday night.

Heavy wet snow and ice accumulations could lead to power outages. * ADDITIONAL DETAILS...Snow will develop this evening and become heavy at times through Sunday. By Sunday evening, the snow will change to rain as an easterly Turnagain Arm wind develops and temperatures quickly rise into the upper 30s. Snow and pockets of freezing rain may linger slight longer for Girdwood before temperatures warm above freezing.

Visibility as low as one half mile. * WHERE...Whittier. * WHEN...Until 9 PM AKST Sunday. * IMPACTS...Power outages and tree damage are likely due to the ice. Travel could be nearly impossible. Roads, and especially bridges and overpasses, will likely become slick and hazardous. Heavy wet snow and ice accumulations could lead to power outages. * ADDITIONAL DETAILS...Snow will develop this evening and become heavy at times through Sunday. By Sunday evening, the snow will change to rain as winds switch to the east and temperatures quickly rise into the upper 30s. The gusty winds may result in localized areas of drifting snow.

events.title: Winter Weather Advisory
events.description: * WHAT...Mixed precipitation expected. Total snow accumulations between 6 and 12 inches and ice accumulations around a light glaze to a few hundredths of an inch. * WHERE...Interior Kenai Peninsula, Skilak Lake, and Turnagain Pass. * WHEN...From 7 PM this evening to 1 PM AKST Monday. * IMPACTS...Travel could be very difficult. The hazardous conditions will impact the Monday morning commute. Roads, and especially bridges and overpasses, will likely become slick and hazardous. Heavy wet snow and ice accumulations could lead to power outages. * ADDITIONAL DETAILS...Snow will develop across the interior Kenai Peninsula by late this evening. Snow will continue through Sunday evening before warmer air begins to move over the region. Snow will likely change to rain. However, pockets of freezing rain are possible in typically colder areas along the Seward Highway from Turnagain Pass to Primrose.

events.title: Winter Weather Advisory
events.description: * WHAT...Mixed precipitation expected. Total snow accumulations between 4 and 8 inches and ice accumulations around a light glaze. * WHERE...SW Kenai Peninsula and Southern Kachemak Bay. * WHEN...From 6 AM Sunday to 10 AM AKST Monday. * IMPACTS...Travel could be very difficult. The hazardous conditions will impact the Monday morning commute. Roads, and especially bridges and overpasses, will likely become slick and hazardous. Heavy wet snow and ice accumulations could lead to power outages. * ADDITIONAL DETAILS...Snow will develop by early Sunday morning and continue into early Monday morning. Warmer air will work in aloft by late Sunday night resulting in areas of mixed snow and freezing rain. The highest snow amounts are likely along the Homer Bluffs with the best chance for freezing rain along the Sterling Highway corridor near Ninilchik and Anchor Point.

events.title: High Surf Warning
events.description: * WHAT...Dangerously large breaking waves 22 to 30 feet. * WHERE...Southwestern Humboldt and Coastal Mendocino Counties. * WHEN...Until 4 AM PST Sunday. . * IMPACTS...Breaking waves can sweep people off jetties and docks, and into dangerous seas. Life-threatening surf conditions and significant beach erosion can be expected. * ADDITIONAL DETAILS...After only brief improvement late Saturday through Sunday, a second large swell is forecast late Sunday through Monday.

location.region: Southwestern Humboldt; Coastal Mendocino

weather.headline: High Surf Warning issued November 14 at 9:08PM PST until November 15 at 4:00AM PST by NWS Eureka CA
weather.description:
* WHAT...Dangerously large breaking waves 22 to 30 feet.

* WHERE...Southwestern Humboldt and Coastal Mendocino Counties.

* WHEN...Until 4 AM PST Sunday. .

* IMPACTS...Breaking waves can sweep people off jetties and
docks, and into dangerous seas. Life-threatening surf
conditions and significant beach erosion can be expected.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...After only brief improvement late
Saturday through Sunday, a second large swell is forecast late
Sunday through Monday.
weather.instruction:
Large breaking waves along the coast will lead to increased wave
run-up on beaches with waves topping and washing over large rocks
and jetties. These large waves can be erratic and unpredictable.
Use extra caution near the surf zone as these large waves will be
capable of sweeping people into the frigid and turbulent ocean
water. Mariners traversing the bar are urged to exercise extreme
caution or stay in port until the threat subsides. Please contact
the U.S. Coast Guard for information regarding harbor and bar
closures.
weather.areaDesc: Southwestern Humboldt; Coastal Mendocino

events.title: High Surf Warning
events.description: * WHAT...For the High Surf Warning, dangerously large breaking waves of 18 to 25 feet with dangerous rip currents. For the High Surf Advisory, large breaking waves of 10 to 15 feet with dangerous rip currents. * WHERE...San Luis Obispo County Beaches and Santa Barbara County Central Coast Beaches. * WHEN...For the High Surf Warning, until 3 AM PST Sunday. For the High Surf Advisory, from 3 AM Sunday to 3 PM PST Tuesday. * IMPACTS...Powerful waves and strong rip currents will pose an exceptional risk of ocean drowning and damage to coastal structures like piers and jetties. Large breaking waves can cause injury, wash people off beaches and rocks, and capsize small boats near shore. * ADDITIONAL DETAILS...A series of west-northwesterly swells will create an extended period of large surf into next week, with the potential for WARNING level surf again late Sunday night through Monday. Areas that may see most significant impacts will be west- northwest facing beaches, with widespread flooding likely at low lying areas such as at Oceano Dunes. Breaking waves may impact the Cayucos and Pismo Beach piers as well as the Morro Bay Harbor entrance.

events.description: * WHAT...For the High Surf Advisory, large breaking waves of 8 to 12 feet, lowering to 7 to 10 feet on Sunday. Occasional larger sets may occur near Ventura Harbor. For the Coastal Flood Advisory, from 4 AM to 4 PM PST Saturday. * IMPACTS...Moderate flooding of sea water is likely over some vulnerable low-lying coastal areas that are normally dry, especially around the time of high tide, including over beach parking lots, bike paths, and harbor walkways. Moderate beach erosion is likely. Isolated damage is unlikely but possible. There is an increased risk for ocean drowning. Rip currents can pull swimmers and surfers out to sea. Large breaking waves can cause injury, wash people off beaches and rocks, and capsize small boats near shore. * ADDITIONAL DETAILS...A series of significant west- northwesterly swells are expected to produce large surf into next week with highest surf and greatest impacts likely peaking Saturday and potentially again Monday. Minor to moderate coastal flooding impacts are possible, especially when largest surf overlaps with peak high tides. Some of these impacts may be moderate to significant beach erosion and shallow flooding of normally dry beaches and walkways.

events.title: Flood Advisory
events.description: * WHAT...Flooding caused by excessive rainfall is expected. * WHERE...Central Fisher County in west central Texas... Northwestern Jones County in west central Texas... * WHEN...Until midnight CST tonight. * IMPACTS...Minor flooding in low-lying and poor drainage areas. * ADDITIONAL DETAILS... - At 854 PM CST, Doppler radar indicated an area of moderate to heavy rain due to thunderstorms across Fisher County, with the area of heavier rainfall moving into northwest Jones County as well. Between 1 and 1.5 inches of rain have fallen. - Additional rainfall amounts up to 1 inch are expected over the area. This additional rain will result in minor flooding. - Some locations that will experience flooding include... Hamlin, Roby, Sylvester, Mccaulley, Longworth, Neinda, Hitson, Busby, The Intersection Of Us-180 And Ranch Road 126, Capitola, Gannon and Tuxedo. - This includes the following Low Water Crossings... crossings along County Road 141. - http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood

events.description: * WHAT...Dangerously large breaking waves of 25 to 35 ft, with occasional sets of 40 to 50 ft at favored breakpoints. * WHERE...All Pacific Coast Beaches. * WHEN...Until 4 AM PST Sunday. * IMPACTS...High tides will result in flooding of low-lying infrastructure, isolated road closures, and coastal erosion. Waves can sweep across the shoreline without warning, pulling people into the sea from beaches, jetties, and rocks.

Mathis, Bluntzer, Calallen...Minor flooding is forecast.

fall below flood stage Monday.

weather.instruction:

deaths occur in vehicles.

Caution is urged when walking near riverbanks.

Please report observed flooding to local emergency services or law
enforcement and request they pass this information to the National
Weather Service when you can do so safely.

Additional information is available at www.weather.gov/crp.

events.title: Flood Warning
events.description: ...The Flood Warning continues for the following rivers in Florida... St Johns River Near Astor affecting Lake and Volusia Counties. .On the St Johns River at Astor, slight rises within Minor Flood Stage are forecast early next week due to a combination of northerly winds, downstream tidal effects, and water from upstream heavy rainfall working north through the basin. For the St. Johns River...including Astor...Minor flooding is forecast. * WHAT...Minor flooding is occurring and minor flooding is forecast. * WHERE...St Johns River near Astor. * WHEN...Until further notice. * IMPACTS...At 2.8 feet, Docks and boat ramps covered at South Moon Fish Camp and approaching sea wall at Blair's Jungle Den. Water approaching sites closest to the river at Fish Tales RV Resort and Astor Landing Campground. Portion of Clair Street covered by river water south of the Butler Boat Ramp. Docks underwater at the Astor Bridge Marina and along Riveredge Drive. Portions of Fox Road are covered with water nearest to the river. Acorn, Hazelnut and Redbud roads are underwater with yards inundated. * ADDITIONAL DETAILS... - At 6:30 PM EST Saturday the stage was 2.6 feet. - Bankfull stage is 2.0 feet. - Recent Activity...The maximum river stage in the 24 hours ending at 6:30 PM EST Saturday was 2.7 feet. - Forecast...The river is expected to remain steady above flood stage at 2.6 feet. - Flood stage is 2.3 feet. - http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
